arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: The veteran's counsel stated the deadline encourages prompt application. He argued it functions like a statute of limitations.
The government's counsel stated the Irwin presumption does not apply. He argued the presumption is rebutted if it does apply.
Chief Justice Roberts questioned the government's position. He highlighted that Congress addressed tolling for disability in other statutes.
Justice Jackson questioned the classification of the deadline. She asked why a conditional filing rule acts like a statute of limitations.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case tests whether a one-year deadline for veterans to claim retroactive disability benefits functions as a statute of limitations. This classification determines if the deadline can be extended for good cause.

sections.heading: How the case got here
paragraphs: The Supreme Court heard oral argument in this case on October 4, 2022.

sources.label: Official Supreme Court Transcript — file page 4, lines 11-21

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: The veteran wants the Court to treat the deadline as a statute of limitations. This allows the deadline to be extended for good cause.
The government wants the Court to treat the deadline as a conditional filing rule. This prevents the deadline from being extended.

sources.label: Official Supreme Court Transcript — file page 25, lines 17-25
Official Supreme Court Transcript — file page 4, lines 23-25

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: The veteran argues the deadline operates like a statute of limitations. It encourages prompt application for retroactive benefits.
The government argues the Irwin presumption does not apply. Even if it does, the presumption is rebutted.

sources.label: Official Supreme Court Transcript — file page 25, lines 17-25
Official Supreme Court Transcript — file page 4, lines 23-25

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Chief Justice Roberts asked if the deadline is the biggest hurdle. He noted Congress addressed tolling for disability in other contexts.
Justice Jackson asked why the deadline operates like a statute of limitations. She questioned if it is just a conditional expansion of the default.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the scope of veterans' rights to retroactive benefits. It clarifies whether strict deadlines can be waived for good cause. The outcome shapes how agencies handle late filings from disabled veterans.
